notes:
Mid-market ecommerce platform focused on checkout personalization and post-purchase support. Initial ask: quick integration using Redwood Hosted API to validate models for relevance and latency. Longer-term: Dedicated (reserved capacity) in EU to satisfy data residency and compliance. Key points from calls:
- Product team cares about embeddings + reranking for product-search and personalization; chat/support is lower qps but tight latency (target p95 < 200ms for 1-2 token steps, end-to-end 300-400ms acceptable).
- Architecture preference: start with Hosted API (fast onboarding + A/B with open models), then migrate to Dedicated once quality/cost profile is stable.
- Data residency/contract: Legal insists on EU-only data processing and audit log retention in EU. Concern about automatic fallback to US-hosted variants — needs explicit controls/policy.
- Multi-region routing tradeoffs discussed: product team ok with EU primary and optional failover to other regions for limited scenarios but wants explicit latency budget and controls.
- SE notes: will run EU-region latency/throughput POC in next 2 weeks; need to test both Redwood-hosted eu-west region and Dedicated pool in same region to compare p95.
- Pricing: they requested example TCO for 12-month commit at 50k ARR vs 200k ARR. Sensitive to token-unit pricing for embeddings; batching/caching recommendations matter.
Direct quotes: "We can prototype on hosted API but can't ship anything until data residency is contractually nailed down."
